glossary.cellulitis: Bacterial infection of the skin and the tissue just beneath it.
glossary.eyelid: The fold of skin that covers and protects the front of the eye.
glossary.ophthalmological emergency: An eye problem that threatens sight or life and needs same-day specialist care.
glossary.facial trauma: Injury to the face, which can let bacteria into the eyelid or orbit.
glossary.orbital bones: The seven bones forming the eye socket: frontal, zygomatic, maxillary, sphenoid, ethmoid, lacrimal, palatine.
glossary.zygomatic: The cheekbone, which forms the outer wall and floor of the orbit.
glossary.palatine: A small bone at the back of the nose that forms a tiny part of the orbit floor.
glossary.maxillary: The upper jaw bone, which forms most of the orbit floor.
glossary.erythema: Redness of the skin from increased blood flow.
glossary.fever: Raised body temperature, usually above 38 degrees C.
glossary.pupils: The black openings in the centre of the iris that let light into the eye.
glossary.red flags: Warning features that suggest a serious diagnosis needing urgent action.
glossary.systemic illness: Being generally unwell, for example fever, lethargy or sepsis, not just a local problem.
glossary.intracranial spread: Infection moving inside the skull, such as to the meninges or brain.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.contrast-enhanced CT: A CT scan after IV dye, which outlines abscesses and inflamed tissue.
glossary.IV antibiotics: Antibiotics given into a vein for faster, higher levels in serious infection.
glossary.broad-spectrum antibiotics: Antibiotics that kill a wide range of bacteria.
glossary.admission: Staying in hospital as an inpatient.
glossary.surgical drainage: An operation to release pus from an abscess.
glossary.contiguous spread: Infection spreading directly into neighbouring tissue.
glossary.insect bite: A bite that breaks the skin and can let bacteria in.
glossary.extraocular muscle: One of the six muscles that move the eyeball.
glossary.orbital veins: Veins draining the eye socket into the cavernous sinus.
